issues.legal_issue: Criminal liability for breach of trust cannot be established beyond reasonable doubt when the accused’s ownership of the disputed property is unresolved and the complainant’s rights first require determination in a civil suit.
material_facts: The accused had a long and intimate association with the complainant’s family and was implicitly trusted by the complainant.
The parties had numerous transactions involving properties that stood in the accused’s name but were alleged to be held for the complainant as benami property.
The accused did not relinquish the disputed property to the complainant and claimed that he had bought it for the use of his disciples and dedicated it to charitable purposes.
By the time of the complaint, the disputed property stood transferred to a trust, which would be a necessary party to a civil dispute over title.
The evidence did not establish whether the accused’s claim to the property was honest or a camouflage for cheating.
The prosecution appeal challenged the High Court’s judgment of acquittal.
issues.conclusion: The complainant’s rights and title to the disputed property had to be established in a civil suit before criminal liability could be satisfactorily adjudicated. Criminal liability was not established beyond reasonable doubt, and the appeal against the acquittal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: For the charge under section 409 of the Indian Penal Code, criminal liability could not be fastened beyond reasonable doubt on this record while ownership and the complainant’s rights in the property remained unresolved. The Court held that the essentially civil dispute had to be decided first; it did not decide whether criminal breach of trust can be committed in respect of immovable property entrusted to an agent.

rule.if: criminal_breach_of_trust_prosecution and appeal_from_acquittal and disputed_property_title_uncertain and extensive_trusted_property_dealings and accused_claims_property_for_trust_or_charity

predicates.criminal_breach_of_trust_prosecution: A person is prosecuted for criminal breach of trust concerning property alleged to have been entrusted to that person.
predicates.appeal_from_acquittal: The prosecution appeals from a judgment acquitting the accused.
predicates.disputed_property_title_uncertain: The evidence does not resolve whether the complainant or the accused owns the disputed property or whether the accused held it for the complainant.
predicates.extensive_trusted_property_dealings: The complainant and the accused had a long relationship of trust and numerous transactions involving property.
predicates.accused_claims_property_for_trust_or_cha: The accused claims that the disputed property was acquired or held for a trust or charitable purpose.

issues.definition: When a breach-of-trust prosecution is appealed from an acquittal and the evidence leaves title to property uncertain amid extensive dealings based on trust and a claim of trust or charitable ownership, criminal liability is not established before civil title is determined.
